title: Lenin Wraps Opening Week at Rs 41.75 Crore, Gives Akhil Akkineni His First Hit
excerpt: The Telugu action drama has crossed Rs 50 crore worldwide in its first week, marking Akhil Akkineni's comeback after a three-year hiatus and his fastest box office milestone.
body:
• Lenin collected Rs 41.75 crore gross in India in its opening week, with Rs 50.92 crore worldwide
  • The film is Akhil Akkineni's first clean hit in his 11-year career and his fastest Rs 50 crore film
  • Andhra Pradesh and Telangana contributed Rs 36.75 crore of the domestic total
  • The film reached breakeven within two days, recovering its Rs 22 crore theatrical target

Telugu action drama Lenin, starring Akhil Akkineni and Bhagyashree Borse, wrapped its opening week at the Indian box office with Rs 41.75 crore gross, according to Pinkvilla. The film's worldwide gross crossed Rs 50.92 crore in seven days, marking the first time in Akhil Akkineni's 11-year career that one of his films has reached the Rs 50 crore milestone.

The Murali Kishor Abburu-directed film collected Rs 2.50 crore on Day 7, maintaining a steady hold after a strong weekend that saw Rs 27.50 crore in its first three days.

Day-by-Day Breakdown

Lenin opened with Rs 7.50 crore on Friday, climbed to Rs 9.25 crore on Saturday, and peaked at Rs 10.75 crore on Sunday. Weekday collections settled at Rs 4.75 crore (Monday), Rs 4 crore (Tuesday), Rs 3 crore (Wednesday), and Rs 2.50 crore (Thursday), according to Pinkvilla's tracking data.

The film earned Rs 9.40 crore from overseas markets in its first week, bringing the worldwide gross to Rs 50.92 crore, Koimoi reported.

A Career-Defining Moment for Akhil Akkineni

Lenin represents a comeback for the 28-year-old actor, who had been absent from screens for three years following the commercial failure of Agent in 2023 and a subsequent injury that required lengthy recovery.

"This is the first time in his 11-year career that Akhil Akkineni has achieved this milestone. Therefore, it also makes it his fastest 50 crore film."

— Koimoi

The film achieved breakeven within its first two days. With a production and promotion budget of approximately Rs 55 crore, the makers had recovered about Rs 30 crore through non-theatrical rights including digital and satellite deals before release. This left a theatrical business value of Rs 20 crore, requiring a distributor share of Rs 22 crore to break even — a target the film crossed by Day 2, according to Sacnilk data.

Regional Performance

The film's collections were heavily concentrated in its home territory. Andhra Pradesh and Telangana contributed Rs 36.75 crore of the domestic total — Rs 16 crore from Andhra Pradesh, Rs 16.50 crore from Nizam (Telangana), and Rs 4.25 crore from the Ceded region, Pinkvilla reported. Karnataka added Rs 4 crore, with the remaining Rs 1 crore from other Indian markets.

Set against the backdrop of Rayalaseema, Lenin follows a protagonist navigating intense family and political conflicts while carving out his own legacy. The narrative draws from the Mahabharata and centres on the annual Bharatham Mitta cultural festival. The film is produced by Nagarjuna Akkineni's Manam Enterprises in association with Suryadevara Naga Vamsi's Sithara Entertainments, with music by Thaman S.

The Diaspora Box Office

The Rs 9.40 crore overseas gross underscores the continued appetite for Telugu cinema among the Indian diaspora, particularly in North America, the Middle East, and Australia. Telugu films have carved out a reliable overseas market in recent years, following the global success of franchises like Baahubali, RRR, and Pushpa.

What's Next

Lenin is expected to see a second-weekend spike that could push its total past the Rs 50 crore mark domestically. The film has a relatively clear run before Thalapathy Vijay's Jana Nayagan enters the South Indian market. The upcoming Hollywood release The Odyssey is primarily targeting IMAX screens, leaving regular theatres largely available for Lenin's continued run.
